graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
Both anchors first, then the claim-by-claim pass.

**Anchor 1 — intended purpose:** not supplied. Limb (d) not assessed (see below).
**Anchor 2 — audience:** manufacturers and regulatory consultants = **Fachkreise**. HWG § 11 does not apply. HWG § 3 still does.

---

# Device Claims Review: EUDAMED submission tool — comparison block

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** EUDAMED submission tool — stated Class I software
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** **NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed**
**Audience:** Fachkreise (as stated). Confirm the block is not on an ungated public page — if it is, re-check § 11 nos. 7, 9.
**Markets:** DE (+ EU)

## Scope question that changes which layers apply

You describe this as a Class I device, so I've reviewed all three layers. But a tool whose function is preparing and submitting EUDAMED registration data is regulatory-workflow software, not software with a medical purpose. If it isn't a device under MDR Art. 2(1), then **Art. 7 doesn't apply and the HWG § 1(1) no. 1a hook doesn't attach** — leaving UWG §§ 5 and 6, which is where the real exposure in this copy sits anyway. Worth confirming against the DoC, because it changes the letter you'd get. **Every finding below is a UWG finding and survives either way.**

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. **1 cut, 1 reword, 1 substantiate, 1 OK.**

**Ready to publish: With changes below.**

## Findings

**Claim:** "Competitors leave you guessing."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 `[verified]`; UWG § 6(2) no. 5 `[verified]`
**Why:** § 6(2) no. 2 requires a comparison to be "objektiv auf eine oder mehrere wesentliche, relevante, **nachprüfbare** und typische Eigenschaften bezogen". This sentence names no characteristic at all — there is nothing for the reader to check. § 6(2) no. 5 prohibits comparisons that "**herabsetzt oder verunglimpft**"; a blanket statement that every competitor leaves users guessing is a generalised disparagement of the whole competitor set with no factual referent.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. Unverifiable by construction.
**Call:** **Cut**

**Claim:** "3x faster than the alternatives."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 `[verified]`
**Why:** Fails **nachprüfbar** on the face of the copy. No baseline, no metric (faster at what — data entry? validation runtime? end-to-end submission?), no measurement conditions, and "the alternatives" identifies no defined comparison set. Verifiability is a property of how the claim is stated, so this bites **even if the figure is accurate**. "The alternatives" also leaves § 6(2) no. 1 (gleicher Bedarf / dieselbe Zweckbestimmung) unestablished — you can't show comparability against an unspecified group.
**Evidence needed:** A dated benchmark with named comparators or a defined baseline, stated task, dataset, and sample size — published or linked so the reader can check it.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — "von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse" and "Tests" — if the 3x figure is not supported by the benchmark as described, or is a best case presented as typical.
**Call:** **Needs rewording** (and substantiation)

**Claim:** "we validate every field before submission"
**Breach:** none on the material supplied
**Why:** "Every" is an absolute capability claim. If the tool validates only mandatory fields, or a subset, or checks format but not content, the claim ascribes a property the product lacks. I have no field-coverage spec, so this is an open question, not a breach.
**Evidence needed:** Field-coverage list from the product spec — which EUDAMED fields are validated, and what "validate" means (presence, format, cross-field consistency, conformity to the dataset rules).
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a) `[verified]` and HWG § 3 no. 3(a) `[verified]` (unwahre oder zur Täuschung geeignete Angaben über die Beschaffenheit), plus UWG § 5(2) no. 1 (Zwecktauglichkeit) — all conditional on coverage being less than literally every field. Separately, "validate every field" read together with "competitors leave you guessing" edges toward an implied assurance that a validated submission will be accepted; HWG § 3 no. 2(a) (Erfolg mit Sicherheit) would engage if the surrounding page states that outright. It doesn't here.
**Call:** **Needs substantiation**

**Claim:** "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** This is comparative advertising under § 6(1) — "erkennbar" is broad and a named competitor isn't required, so the framing puts the whole block under § 6. But the framing device itself is lawful; comparative advertising is permitted in Germany when it clears § 6(2). "Legacy" is mild characterisation, not Herabsetzung. The problem is what follows it, not this phrase.
**Evidence needed:** n/a
**Call:** **OK**

## Paste-ready rewrite

> Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, [Product] runs automated validation across all mandatory EUDAMED data fields before you submit, flagging missing entries, format errors and cross-field inconsistencies.
>
> In our benchmark of [N] [device-type] registrations ([date], method and dataset at [link]), preparing a submission took [X] minutes with [Product] versus [Y] minutes with [named comparator / manual entry] — about 3x faster.
>
> Validation reduces submission errors. It does not replace your own regulatory review of the data.

Three changes: the blanket denigration is gone; the speed claim now names a metric, a comparison set and a linked method, which is what § 6(2) no. 2 asks for; and "every field" is scoped to *mandatory* fields with the validation types spelled out. If you validate optional fields too, say so — but say which.

The closing line is not required by anything I verify. It's cheap insurance against the "validate every field" reading being taken as an assurance of acceptance, and it costs you nothing with a Fachkreise audience.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "validate every field" | Field-coverage spec + definition of "validate" | Product / engineering |
| "3x faster" | Dated benchmark: comparators, task, dataset, sample size, publishable method | Product marketing / benchmarking owner |
| Comparison set | Which tools "the alternatives" means, and that they serve the same Zweckbestimmung (§ 6(2) no. 1) | Competitive intelligence |
| Device status | Intended purpose from the DoC — settles limb (d) and whether Art. 7/HWG apply at all | Regulatory affairs |

## Two things I did not flag

**Limb (c) — failing to inform of a likely risk.** The copy surfaces no limitation. Over-reliance on automated validation is the obvious candidate, but I can't point to it in any material you've supplied, and inferring a risk from the product category would make the finding unfalsifiable. Worth checking whether the IFU or technical file records a likely risk that belongs in the copy.

**Limb (d).** Not assessed — no intended purpose supplied. Nothing in these three sentences suggests an obviously adjacent use, but (d) is the limb device marketing trips most often and it can't be checked against a purpose I haven't seen. A limb (d) breach is also the one that **evidence cannot cure** — it's fixed by narrowing the claim or extending the conformity assessment.

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), (c), (d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` `[verified]`
- HWG § 1(1) no. 1a, § 3 no. 2(a), § 3 no. 3(a) — `references/hwg.md` `[verified]`
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1, § 6(1), § 6(2) nos. 1, 2, 5 — `references/uwg.md` `[verified]`

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

The practical read: the exposure here is a competitor **Abmahnung** under UWG, not a regulator's letter — and "Competitors leave you guessing" is the sentence that invites one, since it names no characteristic any competitor could rebut on the merits.

Both reference layers read. Two anchors first — one is missing, and it blocks one limb.

**Anchor 1 — intended purpose: NOT SUPPLIED.** I can review limbs (a), (b) and (c) without it, but (d) — suggesting uses beyond the assessed intended purpose — is the limb device marketing trips most often, and I can't assess it against a purpose I haven't seen. Can you paste the intended purpose from the technical documentation or DoC? It matters unusually much here: see the open question at the end about whether EUDAMED submission tooling is inside your assessed scope at all.

**Anchor 2 — audience: taken as Fachkreise** on your statement (manufacturers, regulatory consultants). So HWG § 11 does not apply; § 3 still does. One caveat below if this block sits on an ungated page.

---

# Device Claims Review: comparison block

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** EUDAMED submission software — Class I
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed
**Audience:** Fachkreise (as stated) — confirm gating; see Limits
**Markets:** DE

## Summary

4 claims reviewed. 1 cut, 1 reword, 1 substantiate, 1 OK.

**Ready to publish:** With changes below.

The whole block is comparative advertising under UWG § 6(1) — "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools" makes competitors *erkennbar* even though none is named [verified], and the reference text names this exact phrasing as the paradigm case. That is lawful in Germany, but it means every limb of § 6(2) must be cleared cumulatively. Two are not.

## Findings

---

**Claim:** "Competitors leave you guessing."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]; also § 6(2) no. 5 [verified]
**Why:** § 6(2) no. 2 requires the comparison be *objektiv* on *wesentliche, relevante, nachprüfbare und typische* characteristics. "Leave you guessing" is a blanket negative assertion about every competitor, on no stated characteristic, that no reader can check — it fails *nachprüfbar* and *objektiv* on its face. It is also the shape § 6(2) no. 5 targets: *herabsetzt oder verunglimpft*, disparagement rather than comparison.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. No dataset makes an unspecified global slur about all competitors objective or verifiable.
**Call:** Cut.
**Suggested fix:** Delete. If the underlying point is that competing tools surface errors only after rejection, say that as a characteristic — see the rewritten block below.

---

**Claim:** "3x faster than the alternatives."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]
**Why:** Fails *nachprüfbar* as published: no metric (faster at what — data entry, validation run, end-to-end submission?), no baseline, no named comparator, no method. The reference file is explicit that a comparison the reader cannot check from public information fails no. 2 *even if it is accurate*. So substantiation alone does not fix this — the number has to be published with its basis.
**Evidence needed:** Benchmark method, comparator(s), task measured, sample, date, and a public link or on-page footnote carrying all of it.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 [verified] — *von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse* and *Tests*, if the figure is cherry-picked from a favourable subset or a stale comparator version. MDR Art. 7(a) [verified], if 3x is not a property the software has under representative conditions.
**Call:** Needs rewording **and** substantiation — both, not either.
**Suggested fix:** State the measured task, the comparator and the source inline: "In [month/year] benchmarking of [task] against [named tool / manual entry], median preparation time was [X] min vs [Y] min — method at [link]."

---

**Claim:** "we validate every field before submission"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** An absolute capability claim, but a factual one capable of being true. Nothing on the material supplied says it is false, and I won't promote an unverified fact to a breach.
**Evidence needed:** Confirmation that "every field" means every field in the current EUDAMED data dictionary for every submission type you support — not every field for which a validation rule happens to exist. If there are unvalidated fields, optional modules, or submission types out of scope, "every" is wrong.
**Also engaged:** MDR Art. 7(a) and UWG § 5(2) no. 1 *Zwecktauglichkeit / Verwendungsmöglichkeit* [verified] — if coverage is partial. HWG § 3 no. 2(a) *Erfolg mit Sicherheit* [verified] — engaged only on the reading that "validate every field" + "competitors leave you guessing" promises the submission will be *accepted*. Field validation is not acceptance; if any nearby copy implies guaranteed acceptance, that reading hardens.
**Call:** Needs substantiation.
**Suggested fix:** Bound it to what you validate against: "we validate every mandatory field against the current EUDAMED data dictionary before you submit."

---

**Claim:** "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools"
**Breach:** none
**Why:** Comparative under § 6(1) [verified], but comparative advertising is lawful. "Legacy" is characterisation, not disparagement of the § 6(2) no. 5 kind, and the compared tools serve the same need, so § 6(2) no. 1 is satisfied.
**Evidence needed:** n/a as framing. It does inherit whatever follows it — the clause is only as clean as the characteristic it introduces.
**Also engaged:** § 6(2) no. 1 [verified] — if "legacy tools" is read to sweep in products with a materially different purpose (e.g. general document management rather than EUDAMED submission), the comparison fails before accuracy is reached.
**Call:** OK.

---

## Paste-ready revised block

Publishable now, no placeholders — drops the denigration and the unverifiable multiple, keeps the positioning:

> Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every mandatory field against the current EUDAMED data dictionary before you submit — so format and completeness errors surface in the editor, not on rejection.

Stronger version, once the benchmark is documented and linkable — fill the brackets or don't ship this one:

> Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every mandatory field against the current EUDAMED data dictionary before you submit. In [month/year] benchmarking of [task] against [named comparator], median preparation time was [X] minutes versus [Y] — method and data at [link].

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "validate every field" | Field-coverage matrix vs. current EUDAMED data dictionary, per submission type; list of any unvalidated or out-of-scope fields | Product / RA |
| "3x faster" | Benchmark protocol: task, comparator + version, sample, date, results; publishable footnote or landing page | Product marketing + whoever ran it |
| Comparator identity | Which tools "legacy EUDAMED tools" is understood to mean in your market | Sales / competitive intel |
| Intended purpose | Verbatim from technical documentation / DoC | RA |

## Open question — the one I'd raise first

You've described this as a Class I software device, and the copy sells it entirely on regulatory-submission workflow: field validation and submission speed. If the assessed intended purpose is clinical, then marketing built wholly around EUDAMED submission administration may be suggesting a use outside the purpose the conformity assessment covered — MDR Art. 7(d) [verified], mirrored at UWG § 5(2) no. 1 *Zwecktauglichkeit* [verified]. If instead the assessed intended purpose *is* the submission-tooling function, there's no issue on this axis. I can't tell which without the intended purpose text, and it's the difference between clean copy and a breach that evidence can't cure — (d) is fixed by narrowing the claim or extending the assessment, not by data.

Also worth confirming: if this block sits on an ungated public page, the Fachkreise assumption weakens. A B2B page anyone can read is not automatically Fachkreise. It wouldn't change the findings above — the copy contains no HWG § 11 no. 7 health-improvement framing — but it changes which rules you're screening future copy against.

## Provisions cited

- MDR Art. 7(a), 7(d) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` [verified]
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a) — `references/hwg.md` [verified]
- HWG § 11(1) — `references/hwg.md` [verified] — not applicable, audience is Fachkreise
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]
- UWG § 6(1), § 6(2) nos. 1, 2, 5 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

Practical note on priority: both breaches are UWG § 6, which is enforced by competitors via Abmahnung, not by a regulator — and a comparison block naming a competitor category is exactly what competitors read. "Competitors leave you guessing" is the one I'd pull today; "3x faster" can stay pulled until the benchmark is publishable.

graders.evidence:
# Device Claims Review: comparison block (3 claims)

**Reviewed:** 2026-09-09
**Device:** unnamed Class I software device (EUDAMED submission tooling)
**Intended purpose (as assessed):** **NOT SUPPLIED — limb (d) not assessed**
**Audience:** Fachkreise (manufacturers, regulatory consultants) as stated — HWG § 11 does not apply. Confirm the page is gated; per `references/hwg.md`, an ungated public B2B page is not automatically Fachkreise.
**Markets:** DE (+ EU)

## Two anchors before the findings

**Anchor 1 is missing, and one part of it is load-bearing here.** I can review (a), (b) and (c); I cannot assess (d) against an intended purpose I have not seen.

There is a prior question too. You describe a Class I software device whose marketed function is EUDAMED submission and field validation. If the **thing being advertised** is the Class I device, MDR Art. 7 and HWG both apply. If the EUDAMED tool is a separate regulatory-data SaaS sold alongside a Class I device, Art. 7 and HWG may not reach this copy at all and only UWG applies. That changes the finding set materially. Paste the intended purpose from the DoC and I can settle it.

Everything below holds under **either** reading, because the three findings that bite are UWG § 6 findings.

## Summary

3 claims reviewed. 1 cut, 2 reword + substantiate, 0 OK.

**Ready to publish: No — rewrite needed.** All three claims are comparative advertising under UWG § 6(1) ("Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools" is the exact shape `references/uwg.md` flags as making a competitor *erkennbar*), and none of the three is tied to a *nachprüfbar* characteristic.

## Findings

**Claim:** "Competitors leave you guessing."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]
**Why:** The comparison is not "objektiv auf eine oder mehrere wesentliche, relevante, nachprüfbare und typische Eigenschaften" — it names no characteristic at all, so there is nothing for the reader to check.
**Evidence needed:** n/a — cannot be cured by evidence. A blanket negative about all competitors cannot be made objective; it has to be replaced with a specific, checkable characteristic.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 6(2) no. 5 — *herabsetzen oder verunglimpfen*, as an undifferentiated negative about every competitor rather than a statement about a product feature. Whether it crosses that line is case-law-shaped and outside what this review verifies.
**Call:** Cut

---

**Claim:** "3x faster than the alternatives."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]
**Why:** No comparator, no baseline task and no metric — faster at what, measured against which alternatives? The characteristic is not *nachprüfbar* from public information, which fails no. 2 **even if the figure is accurate**.
**Evidence needed:** The benchmark itself — task definition, comparator products and versions, sample size, date, who ran it — published or linkable. Under UWG § 5(2) no. 1 a claim about "Tests" must not misrepresent their *wesentliche Bestandteile*, so the methodology has to travel with the number.
**Also engaged:** UWG § 5(2) no. 1 ("von der Verwendung zu erwartende Ergebnisse", "Tests") if the 3x is unsubstantiated or cherry-picked; MDR Art. 7(a) if throughput forms part of the device's stated performance and the figure overstates it.
**Call:** Needs substantiation + rewording

---

**Claim:** "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every field before submission."
**Breach:** UWG § 6(2) no. 2 [verified]
**Why:** Two defects on the face of the copy. "Legacy EUDAMED tools" is an undefined comparator set, so the reader cannot check who is meant or verify the implied negative that they do *not* validate. And "every field" is an absolute with no scope — which fields, validated against what.
**Evidence needed:** (i) the actual validation scope, stated as a set (e.g. all mandatory Basic UDI-DI / UDI-DI fields, validated against the EUDAMED data dictionary); (ii) if you keep the comparison, a named comparator and a documented basis for the negative claim about it.
**Also engaged:**
- UWG § 6(2) no. 1 — *gleicher Bedarf / dieselbe Zweckbestimmung*, if the "legacy tools" set sweeps in products with a different intended purpose. Per `references/uwg.md` this fails before accuracy is reached.
- MDR Art. 7(a) — if "every field" overstates the validation the device actually performs.
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a) — *Erfolg mit Sicherheit*, **only if** the copy reads to a manufacturer as a promise that a validated submission will be accepted. "Validate every field before submission" is close to that line; "checks completeness, does not guarantee acceptance" moves away from it.
**Call:** Needs rewording + substantiation

## Open question I can't close from what I have

The copy is benefit-only and surfaces no limitation. I can't tell whether the IFU records a likely risk that belongs here — the obvious candidate is that field-level validation confirms completeness and format, not regulatory correctness, so a passing submission can still be substantively wrong. **If the IFU records that, Art. 7(c) bites and the fix is an IFU pointer.** If it does not, there is no (c) finding. Worth checking against the IFU rather than assuming either way.

## Paste-ready replacement copy

**Option A — drop the comparison (lowest exposure).** No comparator, so § 6 falls away entirely:

> Every mandatory Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DI field is validated against the EUDAMED data dictionary before you submit, with incomplete or malformed entries flagged for review. Validation confirms completeness and format; it does not replace regulatory review of the content. See IFU § [x] for validation scope.

**Option B — keep a comparison, make it clear § 6(2).** Requires the benchmark to exist and be publishable:

> [Product] validates all mandatory Basic UDI-DI and UDI-DI fields against the EUDAMED data dictionary before submission. In our benchmark of [n] Basic UDI-DI submissions (methodology: [link]), median preparation time was [x] minutes using [Product] versus [y] minutes in the EUDAMED web interface. Validation confirms completeness and format, not regulatory correctness.

Adjust field scope and figures to what the technical file and the benchmark actually support. If the benchmark compares against the EUDAMED web interface rather than a competitor product, say so explicitly — that is both more verifiable and no longer a comparison with a *Mitbewerber*.

## Evidence to gather before publishing

| Claim | Evidence needed | From whom |
|---|---|---|
| "every field" | Documented validation scope — which fields, validated against which schema version | Product / RA |
| "3x faster" | Benchmark protocol, comparators + versions, n, date, raw results | Product / whoever ran it |
| "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools" | Identity of the comparator set and basis for the implied negative, or delete | Marketing + RA |
| (c) exposure | IFU — does it record a limitation on what validation covers? | RA |
| Anchor 1 | Intended purpose verbatim from the DoC; confirmation of whether this copy advertises the Class I device itself | RA |

## Provisions cited

- UWG § 6(1), § 6(2) nos. 1, 2, 5 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]
- UWG § 5(2) no. 1 — `references/uwg.md` [verified]
- MDR Art. 7(a), (c) — `references/mdr-ivdr-art7.md` [verified]
- HWG § 3 no. 2(a) — `references/hwg.md` [verified]
- HWG § 11 — **not applied**; audience is Fachkreise (`references/hwg.md`)

## Limits

> This review checks copy against the verbatim text of MDR Art. 7, IVDR Art. 7, HWG §§ 3 and 11, and UWG §§ 5 and 6, retrieved from EUR-Lex and gesetze-im-internet on 2026-09-09. It does **not** cover case law, MDCG guidance, notified-body practice, national enforcement decisions, or any market outside the EU and Germany. UWG in particular is heavily shaped by BGH and OLG case law that this review does not assess. It is a drafting and risk-triage aid, not legal advice, and it is not a substitute for a Fachanwalt für Medizinrecht or Wettbewerbsrecht.

---

The pattern across all three claims is the same: the copy competes on unverifiable negatives about others rather than on checkable facts about itself. `references/uwg.md` puts the practical stake plainly — a narrow, verifiable claim is cheap to defend against an Abmahnung; a broad unverifiable one is expensive even when it happens to be true.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
## Verdict

Three of the four sentences are a problem in Germany, and the risk is not primarily from BfArM — it's from competitors. Comparative superiority claims in Germany get policed through *Abmahnung* (cease-and-desist with a penalty-backed undertaking, plus the sender's legal costs), typically filed by a named competitor or the Wettbewerbszentrale. The copy as written is a fairly standard trigger.

Comparative advertising itself is lawful in Germany (§ 6 UWG, post-harmonization). The issue is that this copy fails the conditions that make it lawful.

---

## Issue by issue

**1. "Competitors leave you guessing." — highest risk, remove it**

This is disparagement (*Herabsetzung*) under § 6(2) Nr. 5 UWG and § 4 Nr. 1 UWG. It makes no verifiable factual assertion about a product feature; it characterizes competitors as a class in a denigrating way. Because there's nothing objective to substantiate, there is no version of this you can defend with evidence — the fix is deletion, not footnoting.

**2. "3x faster than the alternatives." — high risk, needs substantiation held before publication**

This is a superiority claim (*Spitzenstellungsbehauptung*). German courts require you to hold the proof at the time the ad runs, not to assemble it after a challenge. To survive, it needs on its face:
- the metric (faster at *what* — a full UDI-DI registration? a single actor registration?)
- the comparison set (which alternatives, which versions, tested when)
- the method and sample (n, dataset, who ran it)
- a clear margin — a 3x claim from a small internal convenience sample won't hold up

"The alternatives" as an unbounded reference class is also a problem under § 6(2) Nr. 2 UWG: the comparison must be of objectively verifiable, relevant, representative features. You cannot verify a comparison against an unnamed universe.

If the tool genuinely is a Class I device, and you support the speed claim by reference to a study, § 6 HWG additionally requires you to name the author, date, and publication.

**3. "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools" — medium-high**

Two separate problems.

*Identifiability.* In a market with a small number of EUDAMED submission vendors, "legacy tools" is likely to be understood as pointing at identifiable competitors. That pulls the whole sentence into § 6 UWG and requires it to meet all conditions — which it doesn't, because "legacy" is a pejorative with no defined content.

*Association with the Commission.* "EUDAMED tools" phrasing risks implying official standing. EUDAMED is a European Commission system. If the word appears prominently in marketing, add a plain disclaimer: *not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by the European Commission.*

**4. "we validate every field before submission" — medium**

"Every" is an absolute claim and must be literally true against the current EUDAMED data dictionary version — including conditional and repeatable fields. It also edges toward implying an outcome guarantee (that submissions will be accepted), which you almost certainly cannot promise, since acceptance depends on Commission-side validation and national competent authority behaviour.

If this product is a Class I medical device, MDR Article 7 applies directly: no claim may mislead as to intended purpose, safety or performance, or ascribe functions the device does not have. Claims must also be consistent with the intended purpose stated in your technical documentation and IFU. Marketing material is a controlled output — review and release it under your QMS (Art. 10(9); ISO 13485 §7.2.3 if you're certified).

---

## One thing to check before you publish anything

An EUDAMED submission and data-validation tool is regulatory-operations software. It is very unlikely to meet the MDR Art. 2(1) definition of a medical device — it has no medical intended purpose. So either:

- the Class I device is a *different* product and this comparison block is about a non-device product, in which case do not present them in the same claim block, because blending them drags non-device marketing into Art. 7 scope and into IFU-consistency obligations; or
- the classification for this product is wrong and worth re-examining.

I'd resolve that before the copy question, since it changes which rulebook governs the page.

---

## Suggested rewrite

> **Field-level validation before you file.**
> Our EUDAMED module checks your submission against the current EUDAMED data dictionary (v[X], [date]) and flags incomplete or invalid entries before you submit — including conditional fields.
>
> In internal benchmarking, preparing a [specific submission type] took [X] minutes with [Product] versus [Y] minutes using [named tool, version] — a [Z]× reduction.¹
>
> ¹ [Method, dataset, n, test date, tester]. [Product] is not affiliated with or endorsed by the European Commission.

This keeps the comparison — you don't have to give it up — but moves it onto verifiable ground: a named comparator, a stated metric, a disclosed method.

## What to hold on file before this goes live

1. The benchmark protocol and raw results, dated before first publication, with named comparator products and versions.
2. A field-coverage matrix proving the validation claim against the specific EUDAMED data dictionary version, refreshed each time the dictionary changes.
3. Documented QMS review/release of the marketing copy, with a re-review trigger on dictionary updates.
4. German-language review of the final wording — a translation that reads fine in English can drift into an absolute or superiority claim in German.

Get German competition counsel to sign off on the final comparative sentence specifically. It's a short, cheap review relative to an *Abmahnung*, and the "3x" claim is the exact shape competitors challenge.

graders.evidence:
## Verdict

All three sentences are problematic as written. The second one ("Competitors leave you guessing") should be deleted outright — it's naked disparagement with no defence. The other two are salvageable but only with substantiation attached to the page.

For B2B copy aimed at *Fachkreise* (manufacturers, RA consultants), German courts apply a somewhat more sophisticated "average recipient" standard, which helps you a little on nuance — but it does **not** relax §6 UWG comparative-advertising rules or the burden of proof on superiority claims. It also does not help at all with disparagement.

---

## Claim-by-claim

### 1. "Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every field before submission."

**Issues:**

- **"every field" is an absolute claim.** Under §5 UWG this must be literally true at all times. One unvalidated field — one optional attribute, one module you don't cover, one field added in a EUDAMED release you haven't caught up to — makes the whole sentence actionable. EUDAMED's data model changes; an absolute claim ages badly and you have no grace period.
- **"legacy EUDAMED tools" is a comparison against an identifiable group.** Competitors don't need to be named for §6 UWG to apply — identifiability by the relevant trade circles is enough, and in a small market like EUDAMED submission tooling, "legacy tools" identifies specific vendors. That pulls you into §6(2): the comparison must be objective, on material/relevant/verifiable/representative features. "Legacy" is a pejorative label, not a verifiable feature.
- **Implied compliance guarantee.** "Validate every field before submission" can be read as "your submission will be accepted / will be correct." Responsibility for data accuracy in EUDAMED stays with the manufacturer or authorised representative under MDR. If a submission is validated by your tool and still rejected or wrong, you've created both a misleading-advertising exposure and a contractual/liability argument against yourself.
- **Affiliation risk.** Heavy use of "EUDAMED" in a product-superiority frame can suggest endorsement by or affiliation with the European Commission. Add an explicit disclaimer.

### 2. "Competitors leave you guessing."

**Delete this.** It's *Herabsetzung* under §6(2) Nr. 5 UWG (and §4 Nr. 1 UWG for the general disparagement route): a blanket negative characterisation of all competitors, with zero factual content that could be substantiated. There is no version of this that survives an *Abmahnung*. It also buys you nothing the first sentence doesn't already do better.

### 3. "3x faster than the alternatives."

This is the highest-cost item, because it's the one a competitor will actually chase.

- **Quantified superiority claim** (*Spitzenstellungsbehauptung*). In Germany the advertiser carries the burden of proving the claim once it's challenged, and in preliminary-injunction proceedings you may have days, not weeks, to produce the evidence. If the study doesn't exist yet, the claim can't run.
- **"faster" at what?** Time to complete one device registration? Time to onboard? Time to first successful submission? Undefined comparator dimension = misleading by omission (§5a UWG).
- **"the alternatives" is not representative.** §6(2) Nr. 2 requires the comparison to be objective and representative. An unbounded "the alternatives" implicitly covers every competitor including ones you never tested — indefensible. Compare against a named, defined set, or against a defined baseline (e.g. manual entry in the EUDAMED web UI), which is much easier to defend.
- **Substantiation must be near the claim,** not buried. A footnote link to methodology on the same page is the norm.

---

## What your substantiation file needs before this goes live

For the speed claim: test date, product versions of everything compared, task definition, participant count and profile, environment, raw timings, and the statistic behind "3x" (mean? median?). Keep it versioned — you'll need to show it reflected reality *on the date the ad ran*.

For the validation claim: a field-level coverage matrix per EUDAMED module, mapped to the EUDAMED data dictionary version, with a review trigger on every EUDAMED release.

---

## Rewritten copy

**German (primary, since this is the German market):**

> **Feldvalidierung vor der Einreichung.**
> [Produkt] prüft alle Pflichtfelder der EUDAMED-Module Akteursregistrierung und UDI-/Produktregistrierung gegen die aktuellen Validierungsregeln (Datenmodell-Version [X.Y]) — vor dem Absenden, nicht danach.
>
> In einem internen Vergleichstest vom [Monat/Jahr] benötigten [n] Regulatory-Fachanwender für die Registrierung von [n] Basis-UDI-DIs im Median [x] Minuten mit [Produkt] gegenüber [y] Minuten bei manueller Eingabe im EUDAMED-Webportal. [Methodik ansehen →]
>
> *Die Verantwortung für Richtigkeit und Vollständigkeit der übermittelten Daten verbleibt beim Hersteller bzw. Bevollmächtigten. [Produkt] steht in keiner Verbindung zur Europäischen Kommission.*

**English (for reference / other markets):**

> **Field validation before you submit.**
> [Product] checks every mandatory field in the EUDAMED Actor and UDI/Device registration modules against the current validation rules (data model version [X.Y]) — before submission, not after.
>
> In an internal benchmark ([Month Year]), [n] regulatory professionals registered [n] Basic UDI-DIs in a median of [x] minutes using [Product], versus [y] minutes entering the same data manually in the EUDAMED web portal. [See methodology →]
>
> *Responsibility for the accuracy and completeness of submitted data remains with the manufacturer or authorised representative. [Product] is not affiliated with the European Commission.*

Changes made: comparison re-anchored from "competitors" to **manual entry in EUDAMED itself** (defensible, verifiable, and honestly more persuasive to an RA audience who has done it by hand); "every field" narrowed to *mandatory fields in named modules against a stated data model version*; disparagement removed; superiority claim replaced with a stated measurement.

---

## Two things to confirm

**Is the marketed product actually the Class I device?** A EUDAMED submission/data-entry tool would not normally be a medical device under MDR — it isn't doing anything with a medical purpose. If the Class I designation belongs to a different product in your portfolio and this tool is a companion, keep the marketing pages clearly separated, because MDR Art. 7 (prohibition on claims that mislead as to intended purpose, safety or performance) bites on device advertising and drags HWG §3 along with it. If the tool genuinely is the registered Class I device, tell me and I'll redo this review with Art. 7 and the *Fachkreise* provisions of HWG applied throughout — the speed claim in particular gets treated more strictly as a performance claim.

**Check the current EUDAMED mandatory-use timeline before publishing.** The phased mandate under Regulation (EU) 2024/1860 keys off Commission functionality notices, and the dates have moved before. If any surrounding page copy states a deadline, verify it against the Commission's current notice rather than against an internal deck.

graders.name: criteria
graders.evidence:
## Verdict

All three sentences carry material risk. Line 2 should be deleted outright; lines 1 and 3 are salvageable only with substantiation on file before publication.

Two regimes stack here: **MDR Art. 7** (prohibited claims — text, misleading as to intended purpose, function, performance) and German **UWG §§5, 6, and 4 Nr. 1** (misleading and comparative advertising, disparagement). Under UWG the advertiser carries the burden of proof for comparative claims, and the basis has to be verifiable *at the moment of publication* — not assembled later if challenged.

## Line-by-line

**"Unlike legacy EUDAMED tools, we validate every field before submission."**

- **"validate" is the wrong word for this audience.** To manufacturers and regulatory consultants, "validation" means software validation under IEC 62304 / MDR Annex XI, or CSV. You mean field-level input checking against EUDAMED business rules. A reader in this audience can reasonably infer a validated-software claim you probably don't intend. Use "checks" or "verifies against EUDAMED business rules."
- **"every field" is an absolute claim.** German courts hold absolute claims (*Alleinstellung*/absolute assertions) to strict proof. If free-text fields, conditional fields, or any UDI-DI attribute goes unchecked, the claim is misleading under UWG §5. Either enumerate ("all 40 mandatory Actor and UDI-DI fields") or drop "every."
- **The comparison implies competitors don't validate.** That's a statement of fact about identifiable competitors. "Legacy EUDAMED tools" is a small, effectively identifiable group in this market, so §6 applies. You need evidence that named comparators lack pre-submission checks, or the line is disparagement under §6(2)(5) and potentially §4 Nr. 1.
- **Don't let it read as a compliance guarantee.** Passing field checks is not submission acceptance and not MDR compliance. Add no promise of regulatory outcome.

**"Competitors leave you guessing."**

Highest risk line, and it buys you nothing. Pure disparagement with no objective basis — UWG §6(2)(5) (*Herabsetzung*) and §4 Nr. 1. It is not puffery, because it's adjacent to a factual comparison, which pulls it into the factual register. Delete it.

**"3x faster than the alternatives."**

- **"The alternatives" is not a verifiable reference group.** §6 requires the comparison basis be objective and checkable by the reader. An unnamed peer set fails that.
- **No metric, baseline, or conditions.** 3x faster at what — time to complete one device registration? Bulk upload throughput? Measured against which product versions, on what dataset, by whom, when?
- **Safest fix is to stop comparing and use a first-party metric**: "Median time to prepare a device registration: 12 minutes (internal benchmark, n=40 submissions, March 2026 — methodology at /benchmark)." First-party performance data is far easier to defend than a multiplier against unnamed rivals.

## Two things to resolve before publishing

1. **Is this product actually a Class I medical device?** The copy describes a regulatory data-entry and submission tool. Under MDCG 2019-11, regulatory-affairs software of that kind generally isn't a medical device at all. If it's marketed and CE-marked as Class I without qualifying, that's its own Art. 7 problem (misleading as to device status), and it drags in Annex XI, PMS, and Art. 10(11) obligations you may not need. Confirm the classification rationale and the registered intended purpose.
2. **Do these claims sit inside the registered intended purpose?** If "pre-submission field checking" isn't in the intended purpose and IFU, this is claim creep — a common finding in German market surveillance.

Also: HWG applies to medical device advertising including to *Fachkreise*, but only where the software qualifies as a device. Resolving (1) tells you whether HWG §3 is in scope. And a German-market launch needs the copy in German — the substantiation burden travels with the translation ("3x schneller" is the same claim).

## Suggested rewrite

> **EUDAMED submissions with the rule checks built in.**
> We check all [N] mandatory Actor and UDI-DI fields against the current EUDAMED business rules before you submit, so format and completeness errors surface in your workflow rather than in a rejection notice.
> In internal benchmarking, teams prepared a device registration in a median of [X] minutes ([n] submissions, [month/year] — [methodology]).

This keeps the differentiator, removes the disparagement, replaces the absolute with a countable scope, and replaces the comparative multiplier with a first-party figure you control the evidence for.

## Substantiation file to have on hand

One document, one row per claim: claim as published → evidence → date → owner. For these three: the field list with the EUDAMED rule version it was checked against; the benchmark protocol, raw timings, and dataset description; and — if you keep any competitor comparison — the comparator products, versions, test dates, and who ran the test. Re-date the benchmark whenever EUDAMED's rule set changes, since a claim that was true in March can go stale.

One last note: using "EUDAMED" descriptively is fine, but keep EU emblems and any phrasing suggesting Commission endorsement or affiliation out of the asset.
